enabled.description: Indicate if the CORS middleware is enabled or not. Missing configuration or an absent enabled key stays disabled; the packaged YAML explicitly enables CORS.

allowedOrigins.description:
Allowed origins, you can have multiple and with port if port is not 80 or 443. This is the global
configuration for all paths. If you want to have different configuration for different paths, you
can use pathPrefixAllowed. The value is a list of strings.
Origins use ASCII/Punycode hosts and ports 0-65535; exact entries retain custom schemes, underscores, and trailing dots.
HTTP/HTTPS DNS wildcards such as https://*.example.com trust every subdomain at every depth, excluding the apex.
Use only organization-controlled trusted subdomains; public/private PSL suffixes and unknown suffixes are rejected.
Credentials remain enabled. Explicit null is supported only by an explicit null entry.
The legacy server-origin fallback remains after allowlist misses, including empty lists.
Enabled CORS validates at startup and before enabling; invalid refresh retains the last valid policy.
 - http://localhost
 - https://*.example.com

allowedMethods.description:
Allowed methods list. The value is a list of strings. The possible value is GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH
This is the global configuration for all paths. If you want to have different configuration for different
paths, you can use pathPrefixAllowed.
 - GET
 - POST

pathPrefixAllowed.description:
CORS configuration per path prefix on a shared gateway. The first raw string prefix match in map order
replaces the global origins and methods; unmatched paths use global settings. Prefixes are not segment-aware:
 /api also matches /api-other. Put more specific prefixes first; map order must be preserved.
Missing per-path origins or methods do not inherit the global values. The server-origin fallback still applies.
The value is a map with the key as the path prefix and the value is another map with allowedOrigins and
allowedMethods. The allowedOrigins is a list of strings and allowedMethods is a list of strings.

Use the above global configuration if you are dealing with a single API in the case of http-sidecar,
proxy server or build the API with light-4j frameworks. If you are using light-gateway with multiple
downstream APIs, you can use the pathPrefixAllowed to set up different CORS configuration for different APIs.


Here is an example in values.yml
cors.pathPrefixAllowed:
  /v1/pets:
    allowedOrigins:
      - https://abc.com
      - https://www.xyz.com
    allowedMethods:
      - GET
      - PUT
      - POST
      - DELETE
  /v1/market:
    allowedOrigins:
      - https://def.com
      - https://abc.com
    allowedMethods:
      - GET
      - POST

allowedOrigins.description: List of allowed exact origins (including custom schemes) or HTTP/HTTPS scoped patterns such as https://*.example.com. Trusts all matching subdomains at every depth, excludes the apex, and rejects public/private PSL suffixes. Replaces global origins; the legacy server-origin fallback remains.

allowedMethods.description: List of allowed methods for CORS requests.
